lvbuild.tagline: ERP for a Costa Rican construction company
lvbuild.problem: A Costa Rican construction company needed a single system for its whole workflow: budgets, client offers, project execution, weekly logs and payroll, warehouse, a store with cash registers, and invoicing.
lvbuild.solution: LvBuild connects that flow end to end: budgets become PDF offers and projects with budget-vs-actual tracking, weekly logs generate payroll, and the system covers the warehouse, the store with cash registers, and invoicing.
lvbuild.role: Sole full-stack developer: business process analysis, data modeling, .NET API, React frontend, automated tests, CI and deployment on Render.

architecture.summary: The API is split into four projects with dependencies pointing inward, toward the domain.
points: Three ADRs document the architecture decisions.

layers.api: Controllers, middleware, authentication, health checks and Swagger.
layers.application: Services holding the business rules, DTOs, validators and interfaces.
layers.domain: Entities and enums; knows nothing about ASP.NET Core or EF Core.
layers.infrastructure: EF Core, repositories, JWT, PDFs with QuestPDF, file storage and demo data.

fitros.tagline: Management platform for gyms and coaching
fitros.problem: Gyms and personal trainers need to assign coaches to clients, build workout routines and weekly training plans, and notify clients, with different levels of access for the owner, admins and coaches.
fitros.solution: FitRos models that hierarchy directly: a .NET API with Owner, Admin and Coach roles, each scoped to what it can manage, and an Angular frontend that consumes it.
fitros.role: Full-stack developer: designed the .NET API with Clean Architecture and the Angular frontend, including authentication, roles and the test suite.

architecture.summary: Clean Architecture split into separate projects, so business rules don't depend on infrastructure.
points: Each use case is a command/handler pair (CQRS-style), which keeps controllers thin and business logic independently testable.

layers.domain: Entities, enums and domain rules, with no external dependencies.

decisions: One command/handler per use case, CQRS-style.
EF Core with PostgreSQL.
JWT authentication with role-based access.
features: Owner, Admin and Coach roles, each with its own scope
Clients, workout routines and weekly training plans

expande.tagline: Production management system for a construction and building-materials company
expande.problem: Soluciones Expande sells construction materials and also carries out construction projects. It needed to control the inventory of several warehouses and its point of sale, its purchases, sales and cash register, and keep a record of each project, all in a single system with reliable data.
expande.solution: A custom web system that centralizes the operation: inventory per warehouse with transfers between warehouses, purchases from suppliers, sales with cash register and invoicing, quotes, reports and the record of construction projects. It is in real use and has been maintained and extended over time to meet the company's needs.
expande.role: Lead full-stack developer: designed the database, the ASP.NET Core API and the Angular frontend, and maintain the system in production. It is the project that has given me the most experience as a developer: working with a company's real data, changing requirements and daily operations.

architecture.summary: The Angular + Tailwind frontend consumes an ASP.NET Core API organized into controllers, services and repositories, which persists to SQL Server with EF Core.

decisions: Repository pattern with interfaces and DTOs.
JWT authentication and API-key middleware for service-to-service calls.
Inventory control by batches and movements (kardex) per warehouse.
Price and cost history for every item.
Audit log of operations.
Encryption of sensitive data.
features: Item catalog with variants and attributes
Inventory per warehouse and transfers between warehouses
Point of sale with cash register opening and closing
expande.privateNote: System in production; the code belongs to Soluciones Expande.

fithouse.tagline: Digitizing client tracking for a gym
fithouse.problem: The gym recorded its clients' data with pen and paper. Records were lost, including sensitive data, weights and each client's progress, and trainers had no reliable information to follow up on.
fithouse.solution: A C# API and an Android app built with Xamarin.Forms on SQL Server, where trainers record each client's data month by month, review their progress to make data-driven decisions, and publish routines so clients can follow a plan.
fithouse.role: I built the entire project as my thesis for the Licentiate in Computer Science with an emphasis in Software Application Development: the C# API, the Xamarin.Forms Android app and the SQL Server database. I also wrote the academic document and defended the project before the examining panel, earning an outstanding grade that allowed me to graduate with honors.

architecture.summary: A C# API and a Xamarin.Forms Android app following the MVC pattern, with SQL Server as the database.

features: Monthly record of each client's data: weight, measurements and progress
Access for the gym's different trainers

vcbike.tagline: Inventory, sales and repair system for a bicycle shop
vcbike.problem: VCBikeService sells cycling products and accessories and also repairs bicycles. It needed to control its inventory and its purchase and sale prices, and to calculate the real cost of each repair based on the products used.
vcbike.solution: A C# desktop application with Windows Forms and SQL Server that manages the full inventory: product intake with purchase price, sales with sale price and stock control, and a step-by-step record of each repair with the products used to calculate its total price. Invoices and reports are generated with Crystal Reports.
vcbike.role: I built the entire application as my graduation project for the Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering and installed it on the business's computer, where the company used it for its daily operations.

architecture.summary: Desktop application following the MVC pattern: the interface in Windows Forms, the logic in C# and SQL Server as the database, with Crystal Reports for invoices and reports.

features: Sales with sale price and stock updates
Step-by-step record of each repair with the products used
Automatic calculation of each repair's total price
Invoices and reports with Crystal Reports

finanzas.tagline: Personal finance app installable on your phone (PWA)
finanzas.problem: Tracking expenses, income, investments and loans from your phone without relying on a paid app, while keeping each person's data private.
finanzas.solution: A PWA that installs on the iPhone or Android home screen like an app, with a Python backend that stores each user's data.
finanzas.role: I built the entire project: the Python API with FastAPI, the database, authentication and the framework-free JavaScript PWA.

architecture.summary: A single server serves both the API and the web app.

decisions: PWA instead of a native app: iOS does not allow native apps or widgets built with Python; the PWA installs with its own icon and in full screen.
One server for the API and the frontend: a single deployment.
SQLite by default and PostgreSQL via DATABASE_URL: zero configuration locally and persistent data in production.
Framework-free JavaScript: a lightweight app that loads fast on the phone.
Service worker: fast loading and basic offline support.
features: Accounts with balances: cash, card, bank and savings
Quick expenses and income from a floating button
Investments and loans with an expected return date and the amount actually received
Dashboard with total balance, the month's income and expenses, and active investments
Multi-user sign-up and login (JWT): each user sees only their own data
